text:
khivraj wrote: Hi all,

Can someone tell me what is the difference between swap zone, SR flip zone and Support that becomes Resistance (and vice versa) after several hits. Are they to be traded in a different way from each other?

first look at above picture

When price reach that line and rebound then we call it support, if the price break that support than it become resistance because common trader teached that way. If price bounce from that line many times than common trader thought it was a strong support or resistance, more touch and rebound than its stronger.

So how IT can manipulate this ancient theory? they make price looks its gonna hold and common trader gonna take their trades and if the price break that SR then the breakout trader ( known for take trade after breaking support or resistance ) jump in and take their trade but IT know where common traders put their SL so IT just take their SL before they reverse price.

so how RTM students take their trade? answer in the picture.

About the swap level i think my knowledge still not good enough to answer that, but all i know is its almost a same concept as SR Flip

author: corsica
text: Hi Sev. I tend to agree. Swap, Flip are the same thing. Broken demand becomes supply and vice versa. And these things happen around a line of support and resistance that we refine with "the kink" aka the FL.

author: Alex001001
text:
Hello everybody!

Today I had a loss on DAX (GER30) and I realy need your help on the following because i think I missunderstood the concept of Engulf and FTRs.

Here you see DAX on 1H and I found some good looking FTR to the left. So far I would say it had everything it needed to be an FTR. Engulf of an obvious low, pullback and then continuing down. Now what made me look at this even more is that price tried to get there and failed two times, leaving a suspicious resistance which i would consider as trick (BSZ). The next break of those highs right into the zone was my entry area for a sell. (also we cleared the way below the CP so this would lead to some very very nice RR.

This is the FTR from the past.

Now what happend is that price just shot through my zone by 5 pips, leaving me confused as it broke my whole plan.

Of course I watched PA on m1 to be sure price is moving down. And indeed there was an engulf by one pip. I smelled blood and sold in the upper part of the zone but got stopped out immediately. This left me confused and looked back in the past to see if I drew my zone wrong.

Looking back I found this. Price stopped right before it touched the end of the zone that lead to the FTR. Is this what is called "true supply"? Should every SL be above this area or was it indeed an engulf? Because price is currently moving more then 100 pips in my -predicted- direction.

Hope you can help me on this one. Thank you guys very much in advance!

Kind regards, Alex
